studyGuide.sectionTitle: Pre- and post-processing in Flow Actions

elements.description: Pre-processing runs when a Flow Action is presented or selected; post-processing runs after successful submission. Pre-processing can execute again on revisit, so defaults must not overwrite intentional edits. Prefer a Declare Expression for a value that should remain derived rather than recalculating it on each action.

elements.text: Worked example: Populate a default meeting only when none was deliberately selected or removed. When the user revisits the form, do not recreate a deleted default.

items.label: Pre- and post-processing in Flow Actions

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Pre- and post-processing configuration for Flow Actions

elements.description: Configure pre/post Data Transforms, activities or supported automations on the Flow Action's Action tab. Post-processing can save one or more savable Data Pages, with parameters and When conditions. Define persistence timing deliberately; displaying a form is not committing its external data.

elements.text: Worked example: On successful submission of a supplier form, save D_Supplier with the supplier ID parameter. Skip the save when the form represents an unchanged draft.

items.label: Pre- and post-processing configuration for Flow Actions

examPitfalls.title: Repeated initialization
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Pre-processing runs only once per case.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Make initialization safe on repeated presentation.

examPitfalls.title: Derived value versus action hook
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Use an activity for every calculated display field.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Prefer a declarative expression when the requirement is a dependency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A form needs default contact data before the user sees it. Which Flow Action hook is appropriate?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Pre-processing prepares data before presentation. Post-processing follows a successful submission.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A user removes a suggested event, leaves the assignment, then returns. Why must the initializer be guarded?

options.text: Pre-processing may run again and recreate the removed default
Post-processing always runs when a browser tab opens

practiceQuiz.rationale: A Flow Action can be presented repeatedly. Initialization must preserve intentional user choices, including removal of a default.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A full-name field must stay synchronized with first and last name throughout processing. Which design should be evaluated first?

options.text: Post-processing activity on every unrelated action
A separate background job per keystroke

practiceQuiz.rationale: A dependent calculated value is declarative. Tying it only to one Flow Action risks stale values outside that action.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which event normally triggers Flow Action post-processing?

options.text: Successful submission of the Flow Action

practiceQuiz.rationale: Post-processing performs wrap-up work after submission; it is not a general page-load hook.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Where are pre- and post-processing references configured for a Flow Action?

options.text: Only in the operator's work group

practiceQuiz.rationale: The Flow Action form's Action tab holds these hooks. Organization and report records have different purposes.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A submitted form must update an external supplier record. Which supported post-processing mechanism fits?

options.text: Save a configured savable Data Page

practiceQuiz.rationale: A savable Data Page executes its save plan against the data source. Display changes alone do not persist external records.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO can be configured for a savable Data Page used in Flow Action post-processing?

options.text: A When condition controlling whether to save
A blanket bypass of external authentication

practiceQuiz.rationale: Parameters identify the data to save; a When condition can make the save conditional. Authentication remains necessary.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A single Flow Action needs to commit two configured data sources after submission. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Both sources must be merged into a ruleset record
Pre-processing guarantees both saves before the form opens
Multiple savable Data Pages can be configured as post-processing actions
Only one Data Page can ever be saved by a Flow Action

practiceQuiz.rationale: Flow Action post-processing supports multiple Data Pages. The single-page restriction of an individual Save Data Page step does not impose the same restriction here.
practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the requirement, then compare the scope and timing of each proposed mechanism.
